Impressionistically, some /H/ tone syllables can be realized on a high‑level pitch, which is transcribed as [44] ..., while other /H/‑tone syllables are realized on a high‑falling contour, which is transcribed as [42] ... Note that there is no contrast between [44] and [42]). On the other hand, /L/‑tone syllables are realized on a low‑rising contour in isolation, which is transcribed as [24] ... 5.2. audit.reasoning: Quote check: both the deciding quote (Sec. 5.1-5.2, pp. 23-24) and the domain quote (Conclusion point 4, pp. 26-27) are verbatim in the Zheng 2023 text we hold layer, and the the primary-stress rule's claim that 'stress'/'accent' never occur in the paper is confirmed by a full-text search for stress/accent (0 hits each). Deciding source: a 2023 peer-reviewed, fieldwork-based 30-pp phonology article — the newest and most detailed of the four Glottolog descriptive refs (no reference grammar exists); CrossRef shows nothing newer. So the 'tonal' coding for the Rongpa variety rests on the best available source, held and quoted. One refinement surfaced: quey1238 has no dialect glottocodes, and the other substantial phonology under this key, Suzuki & Wangmo 2019 (downloaded now, RET 48, open), describes the Lhagang variety as 'word-tone and stress' (pp. 105, 116-118, Table 10 p. 122). Read closely, their 'stress' is an atonalised following syllable

sources.quote: p.105: 'Lhagang Choyu has a word-tone system, distinguishing two types of tone: high and low ... the third syllable of trisyllabic words is always atonal. Stress is also contrastive and is represented with an apostrophe ... In multisyllabic words, stress causes the following syllable to become atonal.' pp.117-118: 'Disyllabic words possessing an atonal second syllable are primarily reduplicated word forms, especially adjectives as well as words with a suffix. sources.locator: p. 105 (overview 'Suprasegmentals'); Section 4 'Suprasegmentals' pp. 116-118; Section 5.1.3 Table 10 p. 122
sources.note: Second Glottolog phonology ref (53 pp) for this glottocode, on the Lhagang variety; unlike Zheng 2023 it posits 'stress' (atonalisation of the following syllable, no minimal pairs, morphologically conditioned) alongside a two-way word-tone system — the only source under quey1238 that uses the word 'stress', so the record's caution field should cite it.
